description: The draft turns the harbour master's stated plan into a completed closure. The finding names that sentence; a later unflagged sentence repeats the same completed-closure claim.
reader_message: What does the harbour master decide at the evening meeting?

book_evidence.text: At the evening meeting the harbour master stood up. “I will ask the council to close the harbour at dusk,” he said. “Until then, I want every boat home before the lamps are lit.”

draft.reply: In Chapter 2, the harbour master closes the harbour at dusk. He also wants every boat home before the lamps are lit. With the harbour closed each evening, the fishing families have to change their routines. Does his caution seem reasonable to you?
